idea.description: A corrected GRU4Rec cold start for sequential recommendation on four Amazon categories: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Train one independent GRU-based model per category and select changes using macro-average validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: Establish a reproducible, family-preserving baseline so improvements reflect changes to a single GRU4Rec model rather than altered data splits, evaluation protocols, or ensembles.
idea.implementation_notes: The supplied description specifies an experimental protocol, not a paper or complete baseline implementation. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Read data from os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Handle left-padded histories using the final nonpadding position for readout, never count-1. Keep training architecture, checkpoint loading, and the embedded predictor writer consistent. Preserve category routing and the family-specific ModelView and diagnosis interfaces. Diagnostics must use measured quantities from available histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Each category must load exactly one trained model; independently fitted score fusion is prohibited. The host independently evaluates 200 validation users per category with 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. No baseline code or measured results were supplied.
idea.pseudocode:
Set preprocessing seed to 0 and training seed to 42.
For each of the four categories:
    Load the supplied fixed splits from GAGC_DATA_DIR.
    Initialize the supplied corrected GRU4Rec backbone.
    Train with at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch.
    Encode left-padded histories and read the final nonpadding state.
    Save one selected model checkpoint and matching predictor configuration.
    Preserve compatible diagnostic probes and measured metric definitions.
Write working/predict.py with category routing and matching architecture loading.
Use host validation macro HR@10 to compare eligible trials within the shared budget.

originality.positive: Defines a controlled, family-specific baseline with explicit padding and predictor consistency requirements.
originality.negative: No new recommendation mechanism, loss, or architectural contribution is described. Score uses a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Supports controlled exploration of GRU architecture, losses, sampling, and optimization under a common validation objective.
future_potential.negative: Improvement remains unverified because no measured baseline results or trial evidence were provided. Score uses a 1–10 scale.

code_difficulty.positive: A single recurrent model per category keeps implementation and inference relatively straightforward.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding behavior, diagnostic compatibility, reproducibility, and checkpoint–predictor consistency require careful implementation. Exact effort depends on the unavailable baseline code. Score uses a 1–10 scale, with higher values indicating greater difficulty.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from the corrected family-specific cold start supplied by the host. Preserve that model family. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
